$comment: The first section of the front page, the latest month (src/lib/latestMonth.ts, drawn by src/components/LatestMonth.astro). It is worked out when the site is built, from the files in public/data, and ships no script. It reads true registrations: the dataset below, never the survivors dataset, and the two are never on one chart. To point it at another dataset, change `dataset` and nothing else. A block that names a field is drawn only where the manifest lists that field as live for the dataset and its slice can be read, so a field the build has not published yet (a block already listed here) leaves no gap and no empty box; the same holds for the whole section when the dataset is not built. `blocks` is the order they are drawn in. kind: total (the month's figure and its change on the same month a year earlier), split (every value of a field, with its share and the change in its share), ranking (the largest values, with their counts and change on a year ago), movers (the values whose count rose most and fell most on a year ago: each side shows `each` values, both months need `minimum` vehicles, and a change smaller than `least` is not a move). `definition` is the address of the definition of what the block counts, on the method page; tests/site/latest-month.test.ts holds each anchor to a heading that exists. `canvas` says which chart the block opens in the canvas: the measure, whether it is broken down by the block's field, the chart type (null: the best fit) and the chart's own settings (src/lib/builder.ts, CHART_PARAMS); tests/site/latest-month.test.ts reads each link back with the canvas's own reader. A change on a year ago is withheld where the same month a year earlier has fewer vehicles than the change floor in config/measures.json (the yoy measure), where the value has no figure then, or where an event that changed how the data is recorded lies between the two months (CLAUDE.md invariant 7). A count the build hides (the small-cell rule) is shown as hidden and is never read as zero. Every text under `words` is a template held to config/narrative/rules.json (kind latest_month) by pipeline/tests/test_site_config.py: it names no figure, year or value of a field, says what the data shows and never why, and is dropped where it cannot be filled.

words.heading: The latest month: {month|month}
words.intro: The newest month this site holds is {month|month}. Each figure is set beside {prior_month|month}, the same month a year earlier.
words.split_up: By {field}, {name} is the largest group: {share} of the vehicles counted in {month|month}, up {points} on {prior_month|month}.
words.split_down: By {field}, {name} is the largest group: {share} of the vehicles counted in {month|month}, down {points} on {prior_month|month}.
words.split_same: By {field}, {name} is the largest group: {share} of the vehicles counted in {month|month}, level with {prior_month|month}.
words.split_alone: By {field}, {name} is the largest group: {share} of the vehicles counted in {month|month}.
words.split_tied: By {field}, {names} are level as the largest groups: {share} each of the vehicles counted in {month|month}.
words.ranking_up: {name} is first by {field}: {counted}, up {change|pct} on the {prior_count} {prior}.
words.ranking_down: {name} is first by {field}: {counted}, down {change|pct} on the {prior_count} {prior}.
words.ranking_same: {name} is first by {field}: {counted}, the same as the {prior_count} {prior}.
words.ranking_tied: {names} are level in first place by {field}: each has {counted}.
words.mover_up: {name} rose most by {field}: {counted}, up {change|pct} on the {prior_count} {prior}.
words.mover_down: {name} fell most by {field}: {counted}, down {change|pct} on the {prior_count} {prior}.
words.movers_floor: A value needs {minimum} vehicles in both months to be compared.
words.no_comparison_reason: The same month a year earlier is missing, has too few vehicles to compare with, or lies across a change in how the data is recorded.
words.caveat: A registration is not a sale, and a past month can be restated by a later export.
words.source_link: How the figures are counted and where they come from
